collectionunit.notes: "Core T1 is characterised by olive to grey clays overlain by lake muds and peats, Five radiocarbon samples from Core TI were obtained to 815 cm (12,860_+250 yr B.P.). No tephras were recorded in this core. A nearly linear relationship is evident between age and depth, with the exception of an increase in sedi- ment accumulation rate above 200 cm depth. The basal clays are assumed to have accumulated relatively rapidly."

site.sitedescription: “The swamp [Tugupugua] is subject to occasional flooding as high runoff after rainfall results in inefficient drainage at the river sink points. There is no drainage of the swamp for cultivation, nor is this agricultural technique practiced elsewhere in the valley. Sweet potato is grown on the slopes around the margin of the valley, near the forest edge. Other crops are grown including Setaria palm ifolia, several Leguminosae and Colocasia esculenta. This is close to the extreme upper limit for Colocasia esculenta cultivation in the highlands (2400 m). Pandanus brosiirws is also a common plant in garden areas as it has not been removed during forest clearance (Plate 2.10). Forest is restricted to the steep and rugged topography and is generally mixed Nothofagus forest, dominating on the eastern ranges, but becoming mixed Podocarpaceae - Nothofagus forest at higher altitude on the western ranges. Subalpine grasslands are found above 3200 m 10 km to the west of the site.”-(Haberle 1993)
